copies.headline: Adam Is Doing This Again, Obviously
copies.body: The defending champ opened 156.3 and 164.7, which is 160.5 a week and first of twelve, and an all-play record of 21-1. One loss. In twenty-two hypothetical games. His luck sits at +0.1 wins, meaning none of this is a gift — he's just scoring more than everyone and collecting the wins that follow. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Kenneth Walker III and Brock Purdy all project for 21 next week, and the roster projects 128 a week, first of twelve. Draft night graded 89, T-2nd. Leif gets him in Week 3 with 135 projected. Condolences.

copies.headline: Worst Draft Grade, Second-Best Scoring
copies.body: Leif's draft night graded out 80 of 100, dead last of 12, and he has responded by putting up 289.7 points, 144.8 a week, second in the league. The all-play is 18-4. That's not a hot schedule, that's just scoring more than almost everybody. Luck sits at +0.4, so the 2-0 is earned. Josh Allen, Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry will do that. The roster projects 124 a week going forward, second of 12, and Week 3 brings Adam. Joey Lunchbox is eating.

copies.headline: CJ's 83-Grade Draft Is Outrunning Itself
copies.body: CJ drafted eighth-best in the room and is somehow third in scoring at 126.4 a game, which is either vindication or theft depending on who you ask. The 14-8 all-play says he's earned most of this, though +0.7 luck means the schedule chipped in. Jonathan Taylor at 21 projected is doing heavy lifting; Tyler Shough starting over Joe Burrow is a sentence nobody expected to type in September. Roster projects 122 a week, fourth of twelve. Week 3 draws Isaac at 121. Real, for now.

copies.headline: 0-2 And Somehow Nobody's Fault
copies.body: Christian is 0-2 with 125.0 points per game, 4th of 12, which is the football equivalent of getting mugged twice on the way home from work. He's allowed 278.5 points against, the 11th-fewest of 12, and sits at -1.0 wins versus expected. The all-play is a flat 11-11, so he's not a fraud, just unpaid. The draft graded 89, T-2nd of 12, and this roster projects 124 a week, 3rd of 12. CeeDee Lamb, Chase Brown, Kittle. Mitchell's next. Cash something.

copies.headline: Peter's 2-0 Is Built On Opponents Missing
copies.body: Peter is undefeated and it has almost nothing to do with Peter. He's averaging 105.9 a game, 8th of 12, and has given up 185.4 points, the fewest in the league — that's not a skill, that's a schedule. The all-play record is 9-13, 41%, and the luck number is +1.2 wins, the league's luckiest. Meanwhile the draft that graded 89 out of 100, best of the 12, now projects 112 a week, 12th of 12. Lamar Jackson and Bijan Robinson deserve better. Logan's up next.

copies.headline: Rezac Scores Fine, Loses Anyway, Again
copies.body: Logan is 0-2 with the worst luck in the league at -1.1 wins below expected, and the 319.8 points against — most in the league — explain it. His all-play record is 12-10, T-4th of 12, which means the scoring is real and the schedule is a mugging. The problem is Week 2's 86.4 after opening at 137.2, and a roster projecting 119 a week, 10th of 12. Jalen Hurts and Justin Jefferson are fine; Saquon Barkley and J.K. Dobbins are both questionable. Peter's next. The dress fits, Logan.

copies.headline: John's Rams Stack Went Quiet Fast
copies.body: The 159.5 in Week 1 looked like a statement; the 81.7 in Week 2 looked like a hostage video. That's a 77.8-point swing in seven days, which is how you go from 4th to 7th without doing anything technically wrong. John's still 5th of 12 in scoring at 120.6 a game and his luck sits at -0.1, so nothing's been stolen from him. The problem is the roster index at 46 and a Week 3 projection of 116 with Puka Nacua and Brock Bowers both out. Kaleb's next. Six-three over Peter won't save him.

copies.headline: Grant Found A Metronome, Not An Engine
copies.body: Grant has scored 116.3 and 115.2, which is either admirable consistency or a team that physically cannot exceed 117. It's working fine so far — 115.8 per game is 6th of 12, the 12-10 all-play says the 1-1 record is honest, and luck of -0.1 means nobody's been robbed. The problem is what's underneath: a draft that graded 80, T-9th of 12, and a roster projecting 119 a week, 9th of 12. Amon-Ra St. Brown at 20 is the whole offense. Zay Flowers is OUT, Goedert DOUBTFUL, Jadarian Price questionable. Week 3 projects 116 against Noah. Of course it does.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 86-Grade Draft Is Projecting Like Nothing
copies.body: The 2023 worst-to-first champ opened with 114.2, followed it with 96.4, and sits at 1-1 with 105.3 a game, 9th of 12. The all-play is 9-13, 41%, T-8th — so this isn't bad luck, it's +0.2 wins of basically nothing. What's stranger is the draft: 86 out of 100, T-4th in the league, and the roster now projects 115 a week, 11th of 12. Ashton Jeanty, Breece Hall, Drake London, Justin Herbert — that group should be scoring more than this. Week 3 projects 119 against John.

copies.headline: Nico Is Out, So Is Mitchell
copies.body: The team name ages badly when Nico Collins is tagged OUT, but Mitchell's 73.0 in Week 2 wasn't a receiver problem, it was a full-roster shutdown that dropped him five spots. Two games, 98.8 per game, 10th of 12, and an all-play of 7-15 that says the 0-2 is mostly earned rather than unlucky at -0.6 wins. The roster is the saving grace: 121 a week projected, 5th of 12, with Jahmyr Gibbs at 25 and Travis Kelce still upright. Week 3 projects 117 against Christian. Start there.

copies.headline: Two Weeks, Same Score, Same Problem
copies.body: Isaac has scored 89.9 and 89.3, which is either remarkable consistency or a broken vending machine. The 89.6 average ranks 11th of 12, the all-play is 5-17, and yet he's 1-1 because his opponents have coughed up the T-2nd-fewest points allowed in the league — luck of +0.5 wins, third-luckiest. The roster isn't the issue: Ja'Marr Chase, Bo Nix and Javonte Williams project this thing at 120 a week, 7th of 12. That's a 30-point gap between what's on the page and what's on the board. Fix the lineup, Isaac.

copies.headline: The Draft Was Fine. The Scores Aren't.
copies.body: Noah drafted well — 86 out of 100, T-4th of 12 — and has turned it into 84.2 and 85.2, an average of 84.7 that ranks 12th of 12. The all-play tells the whole story: 2-20, nine percent, dead last. Luck isn't the culprit at -0.2; he's just not scoring. The roster projects for 120 a week, 6th of 12, which means Achane, Cook and Garrett Wilson are all still in there somewhere. The postseason assassin needs a postseason first. Week 3 projects 122 against Grant.

intro: Adam is the whole board right now: 160.5 per game, a 96% all-play mark, and a luck rating of +0.1 that says he hasn't needed a single favor. Noah is the opposite experiment — 84.7 per game and an all-play of 9%, meaning he'd have lost to basically everyone, every week, and the 0-2 is just honest bookkeeping. The mover worth staring at is Christian, up from 8th to 4th at 0-2, because 125.0 a game and a -1.0 luck score is what getting mugged twice looks like. And if you're arguing John versus Grant, don't — 48.0 to 47.6, identical 1-1 records, identical 54% all-play, and the same 116 projection next week.
